restrictions: Messages of 55 and 63 bytes (the 63-byte one ends in eight zero bytes): one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and the true block length; unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision of two distinct complete messages.

This package (v106): winglock's ef052659 (93.5322) with one change taken from GordoAR (3f8e4e89, 93.0451, and 6a600434): the factor of H1 (i) at margin 1.400, F = 185,350,144 * 5/7 = 132,392,960, instead of 2.000, and the smallest V = 1,057,885 that certifies success 0.39 under ef052659's own success bound (lambda 0.4975807, success 0.3900002; V - 1 gives 0.3899999). The program is ef052659's with only the ledger constants V_RANGE and F_H1 changed (self-test output and public-seed runner observations identical); N, the budgets and the Chernoff exponents scale with V. A preregistered 2^35-batch sample drawn from this run (vd < 1,057,885; the earlier samples drew vd < 1,512,538) passes the three premises. Co-authors: Subflatus3, GordoAR, Jbenisek, tekkac, Th0rgal, leech1996.

ef052659 (winglock) is Subflatus3's 5ca02dfb (93.5576: winglock's c19feef with the stride 2^14 and the pair test by Subflatus3) with two changes by winglock: one stage-A test per four positions with a hit tree, and an early exit in stage C with a continuation and a third budget. From 5ca02dfb and ef81f589 (Subflatus3): order S2K14, four D slots, its preregistered 2^35-batch sample and the premises 0.377 and 1.003, the pair test (generalized here). From c19feef: order S2K, Lemmas A3 and F2, 1-op budgets, the per-batch sample design. From winglock's 18a7fc52, d26a3c5f, 2bb5d604, 098e66f4, 21252124: S8, beta filter, Lemmas B, D, D', exact count, stage C (now the continuation), random word per outer step, Chernoff bound on budgets, X14 = 0. c66f230d (Jbenisek, co-author tekkac), 60f94c5c (Jbenisek), 52bb50ee and 1d5e54ce (Subflatus3), 5266c5ce (leech1996), df8bd46d and 8c81a219 (Th0rgal), ticket 2bf40fb (tekkac).

New in ef052659 (winglock): the quad test (Lemma P4: ((pA0 OR pA1) OR (pA2 OR pA3)) AND B32 with one compare and branch; stage A 70 operations per four positions, 17.5 per batch instead of 18) and a hit tree of masked zero tests (at most 10 operations per stage-B entry, including a 10-operation register spill at the four-batch leaf); the batches entering stages B and C are unchanged. The early exit (Lemma E: W4 = P ^ ROR(P,1) ^ ROR(g1 ^ g1',12) since Y4 is shared; stage C 61 operations instead of 119 + 6; R = 0 implies W4 = 0) with a continuation that recomputes the batch and tests R = 0 exactly (at most 235 operations) under a third budget E_R = ceil(2^-24 * 6001/6000 * N) = 2^76.01 (v106). A register plan with 40 resident registers and eight words kept in memory. A preregistered 2^35-batch sample testing the early-exit premise and reproducing 0.377 and 1.003. Not used: the sub-class, eight-condition rule, E1 test stage and budget premises of 60f94c5c.

Exact part: for every eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7 (Theorem 1), with Y4 in S8; the batches of the order S2K14 (per outer step, member, group g < 37,450 and position i < 2^14, lane l holding the trial with C2.a1 = (7g + l) 2^14 + i) cover every trial exactly once (the last group's lanes 1..6 repeat group 0 and are masked); stage A flags a lane iff its trial satisfies rule A (Lemma A3), the quad test is taken iff some lane taking part in one of four batches is flagged and the hit tree sends exactly the flagged batches to stage B (Lemma P4), stage B iff rule A and the beta filter hold (Lemma F2), stage C computes W4 exactly (Lemma E) and the continuation the XOR differences of digest words 1, 3, 4 and 6 (Lemmas D, D'). Every good trial (R = 0, rule A, filter) has W4 = 0, reaches the continuation and is found unless a budget has halted the run.

Given H1 (ii), a budget halt has probability below exp(-3.1 * 10^6) for stage B (more than E_B - 2^14 entries), exp(-1.4 * 10^5) for stage C (more than E_C - 2^14) and exp(-17.5) for the continuation (more than E_R) (Theorem 2: Chernoff bound over the independent outer steps, after a union bound inside a batch for stage C and the continuation; no independence inside an outer step, member, group or batch is used). Heuristic part: N = 1,057,885 * 2^80 = 2^100.01 trials.

256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers (peak 64, counted on every path of the quad code); seven trials per word in 36-bit lanes; stage A 70 operations per quad of positions (17.5 per batch, including the quad test), stage B 66 plus at most 10 hit-tree operations per entry for at most E_B = ceil(0.377 * 6001/6000 * p_B * V * 2^62 * 37,450) = 2^93.4711 batches (p_B = 0.1992731), stage C 61 per entry for at most E_C = ceil(1.003 * 6001/6000 * N * 2^-11) = 2^89.0173, the continuation at most 235 per entry for at most E_R = 2^76.0130 (count-down budgets: registers cB, cC tested before each group, the memory word cR before each continuation); with the block update (4 per 256 batches), group set-up and end (21 per group), member step (120), X2 table (94 per word, 2^32 + 2^14 words per outer step) and outer step (324): 3.3496 operations per trial, every executed primitive including loads, stores and random words counted as 1; no sorting or lookup by value.

The time bound holds for every value of the coins. Total 2^93.0197120, claimed 93.01972 (2^9301971 < T^100000 < 2^9301972 in exact integers; holds up to 3.349626 operations per trial; budget registers in memory 2^93.0293, a loop over quads 2^93.0648; with the early-exit premise 2^-20, 2^-16 or 2^-12 instead of 2^-24: 93.0199, 93.0213, 93.0441). 5ca02dfb's ledger at this V and F gives 2^93.045076, GordoAR's 3f8e4e89 claim.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step (V * 2^32 words; three 32-bit words of each are used, vc, S15 and S9; D3.d1 = X3 is fixed). Success probability 0.39 holds only under H1, the only heuristic, with parts (i) and (ii). The factor F = 132,392,960 = 2^26.9803 in H1 (i) is assumed; it is the exact model count 185,350,144 divided by 1.4 (margin 1.400, GordoAR's choice; ef052659 used 2.000), recomputed by count_s8.py (proof.md Appendix D), that the organizer experiments do not measure. H1 (ii) asserts three run averages: 0.377 p_B (batches entering stage B) and 1.003 * 2^-11 (rule A with the filter), set by 5ca02dfb's preregistered sample and reproduced by ef052659's, and 2^-24 per trial for rule A, the filter and W4 = 0, fixed before ef052659's 2^35-batch sample, which measured 2^-31.90 (60 events) and passed both tests at 2^-64; v106's preregistered sample drawn from this run passes all three. With the uniform rate the same search gives about 120.2. No full collision is exhibited.

Preprocessing: a declared upper-bound charge (not a premise; H1 and the success bound do not use it) of 2^86 units (2^94.75 word operations) covers all selection of the stored constants, class, rule A, sub-class, filter, stage tests, block constants and hit tree, of the order of the construction, the staged batch, the loop order S2K, the stride 2^14, the pair and quad tests, the early exit and its premise level, the margin 1.400 and V, and of the premise and budget conventions, by c66f230d, 60f94c5c, 52bb50ee, 5266c5ce, 1d5e54ce, c19feef and its predecessors, 5ca02dfb, ef052659, GordoAR and v106, without reliance on run records. Memory 2^100 bytes bounds that preprocessing by its charged work; the search itself uses under 2^42 bytes. Advice under 64 bytes.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's random words (one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step, supplying vc, S15 and S9; D3.d1 = X3), (i) the N = 1,057,885 * 2^80 trials of proof.md Section 4 behave, with respect to the event good (128-bit residual R = 0, rule A, and E1's c1 passes the beta filter), like independent events of probability at least F * 2^-128 each (F = 132,392,960 = 185,350,144 * 5/7 = 2^26.9803, margin 1.400), to the extent that the probability that no trial is good is at most exp(-lambda) + 0.002 with lambda = N * F * 2^-128 = 0.4975807; and (ii) averaged over the V * 2^62 * 37,450 batches of the run (V = 1,057,885) in the order S2K14 of proof.md Section 4, the probability that a batch has a trial taking part in its decisions that satisfies rule A is at most 0.377 * p_B; averaged over the N trials, the probability that a trial satisfies rule A and passes the beta filter is at most 1.003 * 2^-11; and averaged over the N trials, the probability that a trial satisfies rule A, passes the beta filter and has W4 = 0 (proof.md Lemma E: W4 = P ^ ROR(P, 1) ^ ROR(g1 ^ g1', 12), the word that the early exit tests) is at most 2^-24. Here p_B = 36,631,290,006,031 / 183,824,600,268,800 = 0.1992731 and 2^-11 are the exact values of the first two events under the seven-word model M that gives the count of (i), with the distinct trials of a batch independent as in (i). The values 0.377 and 1.003 were set by 5ca02dfb's preregistered decision rule (empirical Bernstein and Lemma C' tests, each at 2^-64, on a grid of 1/1000) from its uniform sample of single batches of this order, and a second preregistered uniform sample of 2^35 batches (ef052659's, disjoint streams) passes the same two tests at both values; the value 2^-24 was fixed before that second sample, after development runs, and the sample passes both tests at it. Those two samples drew vd below 1,512,538; a third preregistered sample of 2^35 batches drawn from this run (vd below 1,057,885) passes all three values. No other sample or run was used to set them. The stage-B value lies below the M value because rule A clusters, and rests on the samples, not on M; the third value has no M value we use and rests on the sample.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Fact P, the construction of Section 2, Y4 in the sub-class S8 of Section 3, the three words vc, S15, S9 from the outer step's own random word and D3.d1 = X3 (so X14 = 0), vd below 1,057,885, w5 and X2 over 2^32 values each, all 65,536 members; batched in the order S2K14 (per outer step, member, group g < 37,450 and position i < 2^14, lane l the trial with C2.a1 = (7g + l) 2^14 + i; the last group's lanes 1..6 masked); rule A as in Lemma A; the filter (c1 AND 00098188) = 00008000; W4 as in Lemma E. Part (ii) concerns averages over all batches and all trials of the run, not single contexts, members, groups or batches.
heuristics.extrapolation: (i) From an exact count under the seven-word model M (proof.md Section 8.1): restricted to the six betas of T6, which the filter contains by Lemma B, the share of solutions of R = 0 with rule A among Y4 in S8 times 2^192 is 185,350,144 * 2^-128, an exact integer from 57 nonzero of 85 outcomes counted by carry automata in exact integer arithmetic without sampling (equal with and without rule A). count_s8.py (proof.md Appendix D; 5ca02dfb's --count code, with the shipped program's constants) recomputes it (about 2 minutes; rerun for this package, identical). winglock's C counter, the Python port and a separately written counter agree exactly; a sampling estimator gives ratio 1.0007 +- 0.0047; every member of S8 has an exact factor of at least 184.57M; the full-class parts equal the published table of c66f230d; brute force at 8-bit words agrees. On real trials, rule-A and filter rates agree with the model at rates 2^-5 to 2^-11, the E1 part has real/model 1.0086 over 2^33.8 trials, E3 partial events of probability about 2^-38 show the counter's S8-versus-rest ratios on real trials as on model draws, and with D3.d1 = X3 the E1 events and the 2^-14 E3 event keep the rates of random D3.d1 (ratios 0.9996 to 1.0002), while the 2^-30 event on the low halves of D1 and D3 has ratio 0.82 +- 0.13 (0.87 +- 0.09 against all random-D3.d1 counts), consistent with equality (2^38 against 2^36 trials). F is the count divided by 1.4 (margin 1.400, GordoAR's choice). (ii) Under M, h1 and c1 are independent uniform words; rule A holds for 2^27 of 2^32 words h1 and the filter for 2^26 of 2^32 words c1, so rule A with the filter has rate exactly 2^-11, and a batch of seven (last group: one) distinct independent trials has a rule-A trial with probability 1 - (31/32)^7 (1/32), giving p_B. The values of (ii) are not extrapolated from M: they are run averages estimated by uniform sampling of the run's own index space (Lemma U), each unit one batch of the run drawn uniformly (outer step with vd, w5, vc, S15, S9 uniform, D3.d1 = X3, a uniform member, group below 37,450 and position below 2^14). 5ca02dfb's preregistered sample (2^35 units, 2^37.8 trials) gave a stage-B share of 0.376590 +- 0.000007 of p_B (empirical Bernstein bound 0.376658 at 2^-64) and rule A with the filter at 1.00006 +- 0.00009 of 2^-11 (bound 1.00096); ef052659's preregistered sample (2^35 units on disjoint streams, the sampler containing 5ca02dfb's verbatim and cross-checked against the counted program's forward computation of real messages on 27 contexts, 540,000 lanes, with verifier digests on every 50th lane and the W4 of all 272 lanes with rule A and the filter compared) gave 0.376587 +- 0.000007 of p_B (bound 0.376654; Lemma C' exponent 1551 at 0.377), 0.99999 +- 0.00009 of 2^-11 (bound 1.00089; exponent 75.8 at 1.003), and rule A, the filter and W4 = 0 for 60 trials, 2^-31.90 per trial (empirical Bernstein bound 2^-28.04; Lemma C' exponent 1015 at 2^-24). Both drew vd below 1,512,538; v106's preregistered sample (2^35 units drawn from this run, vd below 1,057,885, disjoint streams) gave 0.376590 of p_B (bound 0.376658), 0.99997 of 2^-11 (bound 1.00087) and 49 early-exit events (2^-32.19 per trial), passing all three tests. The extrapolation is from these samples to the averages over all 2^100.01 trials and 2^97.21 batches of the run.
heuristics.limitations: The factor of (i) is assumed: F is the exact model count divided by 1.4 (margin 1.400, GordoAR's choice in 3f8e4e89 and 6a600434; the thinnest margin used in this lineage, which used 2.000). V is minimal, so a real rate of the full event below 0.714 of M's would put the success bound below 0.39; the weakest real-trial check (2^-30 event, 0.82 +- 0.13) is 0.8 standard errors above 0.714, and 0.82 together with S8's advantage being only a selection artifact would give 0.89 F. Organizer experiments do not measure the count. M is untested at probability 2^-100.5; real trials were compared with it for events down to about 2^-38 per trial (E1 part real/model 1.0086 over 2^33.8 trials, E3 partial events per outcome, random D3.d1), 2^-30 with D3.d1 = X3 (ratio 0.82 +- 0.13) and about 2^-40 for one call in c66f230d; the full E3 event has too few hits at the sample sizes used to test. M fails inside one context for rule A (clustering); only averages are measured, and part (ii) and Theorem 2 use only such averages. The constants, class and rule A were chosen by c66f230d to maximize a count of this kind; S8 is the best under M of 8,992,320 sub-classes and supplies a factor 1.29 of the margin (the full class with rule A counts 1.089 F >= F); the filter was chosen to contain the heaviest betas; choices that are best under M may favour parameters where M overstates. 37% of the S8 count comes from one beta, 18b0e098. Trials of one outer step share its three coin words and trials of one context differ only in Y4; for (i) their independence is assumed. With D3.d1 = X3, X14 = 0 in every trial (C2 runs with d = 0; X9 = S9 + X3 varies only with S9); the E1 events, the 2^-14 E3 event and the 2^-30 event were measured again in this configuration, the E1-part ratio and the per-outcome 2^-38 E3 partial events were not, and H1 (i) assumes they keep their rates. Part (ii) is estimated from uniform samples of 2^35 batches (2^37.8 trials) of this order, not from the 2^100.0 trials of the run, on the participant side with seeded generators: 5ca02dfb's and ef052659's drew vd below 1,512,538 (their V, a superset of this run's outer steps), v106's was drawn from this run. The stage-B premise exceeds the observed means by a factor of about 1.0011 (about 57 standard errors), so it rests on the samples' size and on the samplers' correctness (each cross-checked against its counted program's forward computation of real messages). The early-exit value 2^-24 is about 2^7.9 above the measurements (W4 is far from uniform: zero for 2^-20.9 of the trials with rule A and the filter) and rests on the samples; up to 2^-20 the claim moves under 0.0002. One organizer run of 256 clustered seeds has a stage-B ratio with expectation about 0.377 and a large spread; it is not evidence for or against this run average. D3.d1 = X3 and the batching change how rule A clusters (S2K 0.5765 p_B, S2K14 0.37659 for the same trials); (ii) measures it in the algorithm's configuration and order, and H1 (i) assumes it does not extend to the event good. The quad test and the early exit leave the stage-B and stage-C entries unchanged (Lemma P4). The organizer experiments see the stage events in 21,504 clustered lanes per run and no continuation. The stride, the quad size and the early-exit value were chosen after exploratory runs (all disclosed in proof.md 8.2). The count program runs on the participant side (about 2 minutes). Run selection: no organizer-run count supports F or the averages of (ii); the experiments' predictions are exact per-seed predicates; every replay and every sample run is reported (proof.md 6, 8.2); nothing was chosen on replay or sample outcomes; after the two earlier samples the program changed only in V_RANGE and F_H1 (which no sample reads), and not after v106's.
